title: Fall back to Cloudflare endpoints when api.fast.com is unreachable
head: c5fb7545b6ce
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A malformed api.fast.com body with a valid JSON prefix bypasses fallback despite jq's parse failure
leads.consequence: jq streams the URL from a complete first JSON object, then exits 5 on trailing non-JSON bytes. The new `|| true` keeps that partial URL in fast_urls, so the -z check does not probe Cloudflare. Workers then use a response known to be malformed; jq also prints its parse diagnostic to stderr. The new test only covers a body with no valid prefix. This is a specific malformed-input edge case, not evidence that api.fast.com actually serves such bodies. Handle nonzero jq status by clearing/discarding its partial output before the fallback check.
leads.triage: already_in_opus_final; corroboration; kept private (Opus judged partial-JSON behaviour reasonable; no evidence the API serves such bodies)

leads.summary: The Run Again tooltip still claims fast.com when the displayed test uses Cloudflare
leads.consequence: After a fallback measurement the button users can hover says `Measure again via fast.com`; a rerun actually first tries fast.com and, when unreachable, measures with Cloudflare. The provider-specific tooltip is misleading in the precise failure case this PR enables. Use neutral `Measure again` (the overlay's own default) or surface the actual provider.

leads.summary: Open speedtest PRs conflict over both the fallback implementation and the new test pathname
leads.consequence: #11197 and this PR both add test/shell.d/network-speedtest-test.sh independently (add/add conflict); #10253 does too. #11197 chooses Cloudflare without a __down?bytes=1000 probe, whereas this PR's test requires that probe, so retaining this test with #11197's implementation fails the download-probe assertion. Separately #10473 replaces the api.fast.com lookup with unconditional Cloudflare, directly conflicts with this PR's fallback logic and, if #10473's code is retained, fails this test's mandatory api.fast.com assertion at line 85. A maintainer must reconcile the implementations and tests if either proposal merges first.
leads.triage: already_in_opus_final; corroboration; published briefly as related open PRs

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up on c5fb7545, reassessing the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13107#issuecomment-5825218762) after the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13107#issuecomment-5825679321).

| Earlier point | Status at c5fb7545 |
|---|---|
| New test passes when uploads or rate output are broken | Resolved |
| Optional: non-JSON 2xx lookup body ends the script before the fallback | Resolved |
| Optional: no lookup timeout, so the panel can show neither result nor error | Partly resolved: the lookup and probe no longer hang, but some cases still outlast the panel's 5 s phase (below) |
| Worker comment does not describe the single Cloudflare URL | Resolved |

**Verified:**
- **Test assertions.** The earlier test passed all three diagnostic mutants (upload POSTs to `__down`, upload exits without traffic, rate lines never printed), 3 of 3 runs each. The updated test fails each of them with a named `not ok` line: `speedtest uploads to the Cloudflare fallback` or `speedtest still prints a rate with the fallback`. The `ignored null byte` warning is gone. The test passes 10 of 10 runs at this head and fails with the fallback removed.
- **Non-JSON lookup bodies.** With `|| true` on the lookup, a 2xx `Bad Gateway`, HTML or JSON-string body now reaches the Cloudflare fallback and exits 0 (base: jq error, exit 5). When the probe also fails, the readable error and exit 1 remain. In stubbed runs with valid fast.com targets, requests, stdout, stderr and exit status are unchanged, and Cloudflare is not contacted.

### Silent lookup drops still outlast the panel's 5 s phase

The reply states that the new timeouts mean "a silently dropped api.fast.com never outlasts the panel's phase". That holds for the lookup step alone: a dropped connection now ends at 3 s (`--connect-timeout 3`). It does not hold for the whole sequence before the first output line:

```text
panel starts omarchy-network-speedtest, 5 s phase timer starts
  lookup   up to 3 s (connect phase) or 5 s (connected, no answer)
  probe    up to 3 s (--max-time 3)
  workers  first rate line after sleep 1
worst case before any output: 3+3+1 = 7 s, or 5+3+1 = 9 s
```

The panel (`shell/plugins/panels/speedtest/Panel.qml`) stops each phase 5 s after launch and treats that stop as expected. It shows an error only for a non-zero exit before then. Measured with real curl 8.22.0 against local test servers (first row: stubbed lookup). Where the probe answers, it was stubbed as an instant success; where it is dropped, real curl ran against a silently dropping server:

| api.fast.com behaviour | Cloudflare probe | First output | Panel sees |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fast lookup failure, e.g. HTTP error (as in #13035) | answers | rate line at 1.02 s | 4 readings |
| Packets silently dropped (SYN or TLS handshake) | answers | rate line at 4.02 s | 1 reading |
| TLS completes, no HTTP answer | answers | rate line at 6.02 s | nothing |
| Packets silently dropped | also dropped | error, exit 1 at 6.03 s | nothing |
| TLS completes, no HTTP answer | also dropped | error, exit 1 at 8.03 s | nothing |

On 4bc1adc8 and base the dropped-packet case gave no output within 12 s, so the lookup and probe no longer hang. That part of the earlier point is resolved.

**Impact:** on a network that silently drops api.fast.com, the panel shows at most one reading. When the connection completes but no answer comes, or Cloudflare is silently dropped too, it shows neither a result nor the readable error, which is the original symptom for these cases. If Cloudflare fails fast instead, the script exits 1 at about 3 s and the panel shows the error.

**Suggested change:** keep lookup, probe and the first 1 s sample under the 5 s phase in the worst case, or start the panel's window at the first sample, as open PR #12866 does. Neither option was tested. Tighter lookup bounds trade off against slow links: issue #12854 reports one healthy api.fast.com call taking 4.71 s.

### Minor notes

- **Optional:** jq's diagnostic still reaches stderr, for example `jq: parse error: Invalid numeric literal at line 1, column 4`. When the probe also fails and the script exits within the phase, the panel would show that line above `Failed to fetch speed test endpoints`, because it displays all of stderr. Adding `2>/dev/null` to the jq call avoids this.
- **Optional:** the panel's Run Again tooltip still reads "Measure again via fast.com" (`Panel.qml:191`), also after a Cloudflare measurement.
- **Optional test improvement:** the new timeouts are not asserted. Removing them, or restoring `--max-time 5` on the probes, still passes 3 of 3 runs. The stub's curl log already records the arguments, so `grep -q -- "--connect-timeout 3 --max-time 5 https://api.fast.com"` would cover the lookup.
- **Related open PRs:** #13239 edits the same worker region and its diff no longer applies to this head. #11197 and #10253 add the same `test/shell.d/network-speedtest-test.sh` path, and #10473 replaces the fast.com lookup entirely.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** head `c5fb7545`, compared with the earlier reviewed head `4bc1adc8` and base `quattro` at `28ceaae7`. Evidence came from source reading, the PR's test and diagnostic mutants in a network-free sandbox, stubbed lookup scenarios, and timing runs with real curl against local servers in the sandbox. No request was made to api.fast.com or speed.cloudflare.com. Timings exclude DNS stalls, which curl counts inside the connect timeout. The panel outcome is inferred from `Panel.qml` source and the measured script timings, not observed in a running panel. The 64 MiB upload size is still untested against the real `__up` endpoint.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
